title: ChatGPT saves Key Stage 3 science teachers about 25 minutes a week of lesson preparation with no evidence of lower quality in a 68-school randomized trial (EEF and NFER, 2024)
summary: In a 2024 trial with 259 science teachers in 68 schools, teachers told to use ChatGPT spent 56.2 minutes a week on lesson preparation against 81.5, with no evidence of lower quality.
account: The Education Endowment Foundation and the Hg Foundation commissioned the National Foundation for Educational Research (NFER) in December 2023 to test whether ChatGPT reduces teachers' workload. In 2024, 259 teachers of Year 7 and Year 8 science from 68 schools took part in a school-randomized trial that lasted ten weeks of the summer term. Teachers in the ChatGPT group were asked to use ChatGPT to prepare lessons and resources and received an online guide. Teachers in the other group were asked not to use any generative AI tool for this work. In weeks six to ten, a typical teacher in the comparison group spent 81.5 minutes a week preparing these lessons and a teacher in the ChatGPT group spent about 56.2 minutes, a saving of 25.3 minutes a week, or 31 percent. An expert panel that did not know which group made each resource found no evidence that the quality of the resources differed. Teachers used ChatGPT mostly for one or two activities per lesson, such as quizzes or new activity ideas. The trial measured teacher time and resource quality and did not measure student learning. NFER published the results on 12 December 2024.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose chatbot. In this trial it was used to help teachers prepare lessons, and the time saving was the purpose of the trial.
